svg.title: Sharing equity: the denominator matters
svg.desc: Two fictional scenarios start with 100 private shares. Transferring five existing shares leaves 95 private and five public shares, out of 100: the public fraction is 5%. Issuing 100 new shares to a public fund leaves 100 private and 100 public shares, out of 200: the public fraction is 50%. For target fraction p and N initial shares, new issuance equals p × N / (1 − p).
